transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Vale (Redwood SE), Sara Iqbal (NimblePay - Head of ML), Tom Rivera (NimblePay - Platform Engineer), Priya Nair (NimblePay - CTO)

Summary (auto):
- 48-hour run data review
- Recommend batch window and concurrency caps
- Next run to validate burst smoothing and fallback behavior
Topics (auto):
1) Throughput vs latency trade-offs
2) Queueing/backpressure during 01:00 batch jobs
3) Security note: VPC + KMS integration next week
4) Pricing for burst capacity
Action items (auto):
- Marcus: push batch tuning to staging
- Sara: share prompts
- Lina: pricing doc

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — is this still a good time for 45 ish minutes?
[00:05] Sara Iqbal: Yep all good, we've carved out time. Quick note, Priya might need to jump at 11:05.
[00:10] Marcus Vale: Cool. I pulled the 48-hour run, it's in the dashboard link I dropped in the chat. The headline: average p99 token latency held, but we saw three pronounced queue spikes.
[00:24] Tom Rivera: Those spikes line up with our nightly settlement job at 01:00 UTC, right? We batch 10k transactions and fan out prompts to the inference path.
[00:30] Marcus Vale: Exactly. When the job fans out, request concurrency shoots from ~50 to ~900 for a couple minutes. Our continuous batching didn't stabilize because most prompts are short — so batch assembler is closing windows early, leading to small batches and lots of contexts. There's also, um, slight KV cache thrashing — KV cash? — yeah that shows up as more memory churn.
[00:48] Sara Iqbal: Right, short prompts, high qps. We can probably change the job to spread the fan-out but that's a nontrivial change to our jobs infra. Prefer if REDWOOD can help smooth it.
[00:58] Lina Park: Totally, that's why we're here. Marc, what are the knob recommendations?
[01:02] Marcus Vale: Two immediate things: bump the continuous-batching window from 15ms to 50-100ms, and add an adaptive max-concurrency cap that lowers concurrency when queue depth hits a threshold — basically backpressure. Also enable prefix-KV caching for the most common prompt header to reduce K-V misses. Note: prefix caching sometimes misfires if prompts vary a lot.
[01:27] Tom Rivera: Curious about latency impact. If we increase the batching window, p50 might improve but p99 could jitter?
[01:33] Marcus Vale: There is a tradeoff. Bigger window increases batch size so throughput goes up and per-token cost down; single-request latency can add 30-80ms depending on batch size. But with our current p99 we have headroom — during spikes p99 actually got worse because the system saturated and queued. So smoothing reduces extreme queuing and net p99 improves in burst scenarios.
[01:56] Priya Nair: Are there any changes needed for the dedicated vs hosted selection? We're evaluating Dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs.
[02:03] Lina Park: For Dedicated we can set stronger concurrency guarantees and reserved GPU pools, and also configure burst capacity for 10-minute windows. Pricing is additive. We'll send details.
[02:12] Sara Iqbal: On the cache note, our prompts are templated but have variable user names, so exact prefix matches are rare. Can Redwood do prefix normalization or a heuristic?
[02:21] Marcus Vale: We can add a lightweight normalizer — strip user tokens, standardize dates — that runs pre-batch. That will improve prefix match rate but needs customer-side consent for token processing.
[02:33] Tom Rivera: Ok that's doable. We'll need the rules first.
[02:37] Lina Park: We'll draft suggested normalization patterns.
[02:41] Marcus Vale: Also saw a couple of model fallbacks during the run — when a node hit OOM we routed to a smaller quantized variant which had slightly different output distribution. Not a big quality regression but flagged in the evals.
[02:57] Sara Iqbal: We noticed slight hallucination variance. Not a showstopper but we want to avoid noisy fallback.
[03:03] Marcus Vale: We can tighten the fallback policy: prefer same-architecture quantized variant and apply a small output smoothing step. Also configure a conservative fallback-only window to avoid frequent flips.
[03:15] Tom Rivera: Instrumentation question — what queue metrics should we add to our dashboard? Right now we only have request rate and GPU utilization.
[03:23] Marcus Vale: Add queue depth over time, batch size distribution, wait_time histogram (how long requests sit before entering a batch), and per-route concurrency. Also add a flag for "burst source" tag so we can correlate to the settlement job.
[03:38] Tom Rivera: We can add those. We'll need the metric names so we don't mis-map.
[03:42] Marcus Vale: I'll provide the metric keys and exemplar Grafana panels.
[03:46] Sara Iqbal: Quick question on encryption — we want to ensure the job's payload never leaves our VPC. You mentioned Redwood Private; how fast can that be stood up?
[03:55] Lina Park: For VPC Private we have an enterprise onboarding process; typical lead time is 4–6 weeks, but we can do a limited VPC peering test in 2 weeks for the pilot. KMS/HSM integration is part of the Private package.
[04:09] Priya Nair: Good to know. Also, compliance: SOC 2 docs — can you resend?
[04:14] Lina Park: Yes will send SOC 2 and our audit summary after the call.
[04:19] Tom Rivera: Back to concurrency cap: do you recommend a static cap or adaptive (based on queue depth)?
[04:25] Marcus Vale: Adaptive is better. Simple algorithm: start with observed baseline concurrency (we saw ~60 steady), set cap to baseline * 8 for bursts but reduce it linearly when queue depth exceeds 2000 requests. We'll tune thresholds after the next run.
[04:40] Sara Iqbal: Can you translate those numbers into expected GPU counts so we can budget?
[04:45] Marcus Vale: Rough calc: for your average prompt length and model, 8x concurrency at peak equals about 6 additional GPU-minutes per 1k requests in a minute. I'll produce a cost projection CSV.
[04:56] Lina Park: On pricing: there's a Dedicated burst add-on; I'll draft pricing scenarios (monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go) and include the numbers Marcus generates.
[05:05] Tom Rivera: Regarding the 48-hour data, one oddity: around 03:12 UTC there was a brief oscillation where queue depth doubled twice in 30s. Any idea?
[05:14] Marcus Vale: That looks like a small cascading retry from your upstream — when a subset of workers received 502s they retried aggressively. We saw the retry TTL cause a feedback loop. Two suggestions: add jittered exponential backoff on client side, and configure a short token bucket rate limiter in the gateway to trim bursts.
[05:33] Sara Iqbal: We'll check the worker retry logic; adding jitter is low effort.
[05:37] Marcus Vale: One more tuning: enable small preferred-batch fill (prefer batches of >=8) — that way the system waits slightly longer for small requests rather than sending 1-2 request batches. That combined with the normalizer should increase mean batch size from 3 to ~12 in spikes.
[05:55] Priya Nair: Any concerns about throughput regression for interactive flows? We have chat flows that need low latency.
[06:01] Marcus Vale: We can route interactive traffic to a latency-first route with minimal batching, and route batch jobs to throughput-optimized route. Smart routing is supported in the platform; you'll need per-route configs.
[06:11] Tom Rivera: What's the rollout plan for the changes? We can't make all changes midpoint through a business week.
[06:16] Lina Park: Proposed plan: 1) Staging tuning (Marcus) by 11/30; 2) 48-hour validation run on staging + production-mirror on 12/01-12/02; 3) Review on 12/03; 4) If green, roll to prod during weekend maintenance window 12/05.
[06:31] Sara Iqbal: Works for us. We might ask for a shorter canary first.
[06:35] Marcus Vale: We'll do a 2-hour canary with traffic shaping before full weekend roll.
[06:39] Priya Nair: And the fallback policy change — will that require re-eval of prompts?
[06:44] Marcus Vale: No, it's a runtime routing change. We'll surface any output deltas via the evals bucket. If you want, we can pin a prompt test suite to run against both variants.
[06:54] Tom Rivera: Yes please. We'll need the test harness spec.
[06:57] Lina Park: I'll attach a lightweight harness template and a benchmark spreadsheet.
[07:02] Sara Iqbal: One last item — security review with our procurement is next week; can you provide an architecture slide that shows VPC peering flow, KMS, audit logs?
[07:11] Lina Park: Absolutely, we'll send a slide plus SOC 2 docs.
[07:15] Marcus Vale: I'll also include the dashboard metric names and an example batch histogram.
[07:19] Priya Nair: Great. Anything else?
[07:22] Lina Park: Quick recap of next steps: Marcus runs tuning by 11/30, Sara shares prompts by 11/30, Lina sends pricing and SOC 2 and architecture slides by 12/02, schedule infra deep-dive for 12/03.
[07:33] Tom Rivera: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:36] Sara Iqbal: Thanks.
[07:38] Marcus Vale: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
